items.title: US Department of Labor publishes proposed rule setting national minimum weekly work search requirement for unemployment insurance
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Employment and Training Administration today announced a proposed rule designed to improve the integrity and accountability of the Federal-State Unemployment Insurance Program by establishing a national minimum weekly work search standard for individuals claiming unemployment insurance benefits. Under the proposed rule, individuals claiming unemployment insurance benefits would be required to complete at least five qualifying work-search activities each week and to report those activities before payment is issued. “The purpose of unemployment insurance is to provide temporary support while people proactively search for a new job or upskill to meet the needs of employers restoring critical supply chains,” said U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “This proposed rule helps jobseekers find work faster and ensures efficient use of taxpayer resources while improving the overall integrity of our unemployment system.”The proposal would also identify a range of modern job search activities beyond employer contacts, including registration and ongoing contact with placement agencies and unions that are specific, identifiable, an

items.title: Post-Employment Conflict of Interest Restrictions; Revision of Departmental Component Designations
items.summary: The U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE) is issuing this final rule to update the name of an existing departmental component that was previously designated for purposes of the one-year post- employment conflict of interest restriction for senior employees.

items.title: Powers of Federal Credit Unions
items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is proposing to amend the NCUA's regulations regarding incidental powers to clarify that federal credit unions (FCUs) are not required to seek an advisory opinion from the NCUA's Office of General Counsel before petitioning the Board to engage in an activity that does not fall within an FCU's preapproved incidental powers.
